Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral lateral displacement of the paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) forming a smooth, widened lower posterior mediastinal mass without vertebral destruction or respiratory symptoms. This radiographic appearance is classic for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (or lymphoma in general) involving the posterior mediastinum, distinguishing it from neurogenic tumors which are typically unilateral and extramedullary hematopoiesis which usually presents with lobulated masses in anemic patients.
